summary: This script sets up a new SQL Server database called SampleDB, creates a Customers table with columns for customer information, populates it with ten sample customer records, and then displays all the data to verify it was inserted correctly.

explanations.3: GO is a batch separator in SQL Server that tells the database to execute all the statements above it before continuing; think of it like hitting 'run' on a chunk of code.
explanations.7: Another GO statement, this time ensuring the USE command (which switches to the SampleDB database) completes before the next batch of statements runs.
explanations.11: IDENTITY(1,1) means SQL Server will automatically assign a unique number to each new customer, starting at 1 and incrementing by 1 each time, so you don't have to manually provide these values.
explanations.17: GO executes the CREATE TABLE statement so the table actually exists in the database before we try to insert data into it.
explanations.31: GO executes all the INSERT statements above it, adding all ten customer rows to the table in one batch.
explanations.35: GO ensures the SELECT query runs after all previous statements are complete, so you see the final populated table.
